title: Полгода без зарплаты  (Six Months Without Pay)

segments.t: After the producer spits out the varnish-covered lamb, a furious Dmitry Nagiyev storms into the kitchen to confront Viktor Barinov, while one of the television crew's cameras remains running on the counter. Listen in Russian first.
Не надо. Ты уже накормил всех.
Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
Now let's examine each line of their conversation and see how the Russian expressions fit together.
'Quickly! Pack everything up fast!' Chef Viktor delivers this line as an emphatic exclamation, putting strong stress on the main word.
'Dima, I will explain everything to you right now.' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular pronoun, showing a close or familiar relationship.
'We will feed your guests properly right away.' Chef Viktor uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
Не надо. Ты уже накормил всех.
'Don't bother. You have already fed everyone.' Dmitry places the negative particle directly before the verb or predicate to negate the statement.
'Open the door, I told you!' In spoken Russian, Dmitry omits unnecessary linking verbs so the key idea lands immediately.
Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
'You are fired! Open the door, I am counting to three.' The past-tense verb ending marks the grammatical gender and number of the subject directly.
'Six months.' Dmitry keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'You are working without a salary.' In spoken Russian, Dmitry omits unnecessary linking verbs so the key idea lands immediately.
'Did you understand me?' Dmitry raises the pitch on the key word to turn this short Russian clause into a direct question.
'He is an absolute madman.' Chef Viktor keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'Yes, all the time!' Lyova keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'I have had enough of this slave driver!' The past-tense verb ending marks the grammatical gender and number of the subject directly. Now let's replay the whole dialogue at natural speed.
Не надо. Ты уже накормил всех.
Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
That completes the explosive confrontation in the kitchen where Nagiyev docks Viktor six months' salary. Listen out for the imperative verbs and colloquial exclamations. See you in the next scene.
